stageA.sourceInspection: All five live primary PDFs were inspected once. Local source hashes matched live paper and file hashes for S1247, S1260, S1384 and S1903. The cached S1899 PDF was a different source and was not used; the actual live attachment was downloaded once, matched live hashes, and was inspected.
stageA.dryRun: The standard no-write apply script stopped at its documented limitation: it cannot derive brand-new multiline population groups before a live write. Separate schema and newline-alignment validation passed for all 70 staged fields and all three population layouts.

classification.S1247: Schema-compatible player prevalence data: pooled psychiatric/psychological disordered-eating prevalence and calculated-EA low-energy-availability prevalence were staged without inventing an all-illness total.
classification.S1260: Schema-compatible prospective player psychiatric prevalence/new-onset data: direct distress values were staged by baseline and follow-up; overlapping symptom categories were not summed.
classification.S1384: Schema-compatible psychiatric diagnoses: MINI values were staged only for the directly reported second-division cohort and sex subgroups.
classification.S1899: Referee cohort, not an eligible current-player extraction record.
classification.S1903: Mental well-being screening-tool development and psychometric validation, with no reportable disorder-prevalence or injury/illness surveillance payload.

apply.mode: additive-only field writes with complete core Tabs 1-4, structured population sync, and source-supported status routing

sourceCoverage.S1247: Primary PDF pp. 1-9; methods, Tables 1-5, Figures 1-3, results, discussion and conclusion. Figure 3's direct 44% values support the stored psychiatric count and prevalence; historical injury was not mapped as surveillance.
sourceCoverage.S1260: Primary PDF pp. 1-8; methods, all validated questionnaire definitions, Tables 1-4, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion. The directly reported Table 2 values support the baseline/follow-up psychiatric rows; the referenced online supplement was not attached.
sourceCoverage.S1384: Primary PDF pp. 1-14; participant methods, Tables 1-4, results, discussion, limitations and conclusion. Direct MINI diagnosis values apply only to the second-division cohort.
sourceCoverage.S1899: Matching live primary PDF pp. 199-214; methods, Tables 1-4, results, discussion and conclusion. Referee-only population confirmed.
sourceCoverage.S1903: Primary PDF pp. 33-45; all three development/validation phases, participant section, psychometric results, discussion, limitations and Appendix A. Tool validity/reliability, rather than reportable surveillance prevalence, confirmed.

caveats.S1247: Psychiatric n=11 is transparently percentage-derived from 44% of 25. Poor mental health, disordered eating and low energy availability overlap, so the audit preserves condition-specific structured values and omits an artificial total.
caveats.S1260: The follow-up symptom incidence denominator varies by symptom; the 80-player response count does not replace those symptom-specific denominators. The seven symptom categories overlap. Historical injury/surgery associations were not treated as injury surveillance.
caveats.S1384: MINI diagnostic categories are comorbid and were not summed. First-division players did not undergo that diagnostic interview, so no all-54 diagnostic total was inferred.
caveats.S1899: A mismatched cached PDF was detected before extraction and replaced by the matching live attachment for this source sweep. The correct referee exclusion has no extraction payload.
caveats.S1903: The paper is a screening-process and psychometric validation study, not a disorder-prevalence or injury/illness surveillance record; no extraction payload was forced.

readyFor: human extraction review for S1247, S1260 and S1384; classification review for S1899 and S1903
